newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka's Finlay says to make Instant Tea.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka's Finlay says to make Instant Tea.

text.p: Sri Lankan tea exporter James Finlay is setting up an instant tea factory aimed at the fast-growing ready-to-drink (RTD) tea market, its chairman said on Thursday.
"We're trying to increase the share of tea in the beverage market," Dickie Juriansz told Reuters in an interview.

"We're not aiming at existing tea drinkers who drink tea in its traditional (hot) form," he said. "We're trying to convert people who drink other beverages out of a bottle or a can or in powdered form. We're offering them the same convenience."
A bottled RTD tea product made in Japan with raw material supplied by the firm, which has managed plantations in the island for over 100 years, was selling well, he said.
The company's RTD tea products will eventually compete against soft drink giants such as Coca-Cola Co. and Pepsi-Cola, he said.

Finlay, one of the Indian Ocean island's top exporters of value-added teas, spent 200 million rupees ($3.47 million) in 1996 on construction and machinery for the Instant Tea factory, which is expected to start trial production in July, Juriansz said.
The factory will produce almost a million kilograms of instant tea or tea concentrate annually when commercial production gets underway, he said.
The company will supply the base material to manufacturers of RTD teas, he said.
The total cost of the project is estimated at 300 million rupees and will mostly be funded by a two-for-one rights issue at 50 rupees, which will raise 250 million rupees, he said.
"Instant tea has been around in the United States for a long time, but it is new in the rest of the world," Juriansz said.

"Tea is seen as a health beverage unlike colas which are seen as being fizzy and with artificial flavouring," he added. "Given a choice people prefer to go for health beverages because they are looking for healthy lifestyles."
